headline.purpose: Section heads (Onion sites, Add an address) and the brand name; 21.6sp medium natively.

title.purpose: Result titles and empty-state heads; the search field's text at this size, weight 400.

body.purpose: Snippets (max 70ch, three lines), explanations, inputs, the browser address.

body-strong.purpose: Buttons, router names, Explore site names.

label.purpose: Trust strip, summary, meta lines, file lists; tabular figures for numbers.

label-strong.purpose: Route badges; the browser's kind label natively (12sp medium).

mono.purpose: Addresses and hashes only, one ellipsised line.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Around a focused search or address field, with the border turning glow. Spread without blur; the only coloured shadow.

shadows.name: hollow-dot
shadows.purpose: Draws an unselected chip's 8px network dot as a ring; removed when the chip is selected.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Every web transition and keyframe entrance (--ease).

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Border, background and colour changes on chips, buttons, the trust strip and fields.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Trust panel opening (fade and 6px drop), chevron turns, the focus ring appearing.

motion.name: duration-enter
motion.purpose: A result new to the list fades in from 0.4 opacity and rises 4px; rows already showing stay still.

motion.name: search-debounce
motion.purpose: Typing pause before a search runs.

motion.name: skeleton-delay
motion.purpose: Skeleton rows appear only when a search takes longer than this; there is no spinner.

motion.name: skeleton-shimmer
motion.purpose: Surface to surface-2 highlight travelling across skeleton bars.

motion.name: connecting-breathe
motion.purpose: A connecting router's dot dims to 0.35 opacity and back.

motion.name: copied-confirm
motion.purpose: How long the copy button shows its green check.

motion.name: browser-open-enter
motion.purpose: Android: the browser scales from 0.94 (pivot 50% / 60%) and fades in over the search page.

motion.name: browser-open-exit
motion.purpose: Android: the search page fades to 0.6 behind the opening browser.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every animation and transition is removed.

narrative.overview:
omnid is one board that every network plugs into: onion sites, I2P, Hyphanet, torrents and the open web, each line labelled with where it leads and lit to show whether it is live and whether the way there is sealed. The board sits on the icon's deep navy and is lit only by the icon's own blues. The metaphor shapes structure, never imagery: there are no cables, sockets or retro hardware anywhere, and the system rejects both a themed "dark web" costume and the generic grey search app.

The feel is calm and quick, built to the bar of Arc Search, Signal and Proton. Density is phone-first and moderate: one column, hairline-separated rows, a single large search field, and a trust strip that states router health in plain words before anything else. Colour is spent on meaning. One accent carries action and selection, glow blue carries focus, and each network owns a hue that appears only as a small dot or a route badge. Depth comes from tone, not shadow.

Light and dark are one token set expressed twice, shared by the web page (`crates/omnid/src/ui/app.css`) and the Android chrome (`res/values*/colors.xml`). Dark is the brand's home: navy ground, moonlit ink. Light is cool paper with navy ink and a stronger blue, so every accent role keeps its contrast. Where the icon's pale glow would vanish on the light ground, the brand mark changes rendition instead of the palette changing hue.
keyCharacteristics: One navy ground shared by the window, system bars, toolbars and page.
One accent for action and selection; glow blue only for focus, the caret and progress.
Network hues confined to 8px dots, route badges and the browser's kind label.
The platform sans on four sizes 1.2 apart; mono only for addresses; tabular figures for data.
Flat tonal surfaces with 1px hairlines; the focus ring is the only coloured shadow.
Pills for state and filters, 14px rounded rectangles for actions, 16px corners for surfaces.
Short, decelerating motion; results update in place.

rules.name: The Dots-and-Badges Rule
rules.body: A network's hue appears only as an 8px dot, a route badge (the hue at 14% behind text in the hue) or the browser's kind label. It is never a chip fill, a row tint, a button or a border.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Selection looks the same on every network: accent at 13% over surface, an accent-tinted border and an accent check. The `glow` token marks focus, the caret and progress, and nothing else.

rules.name: The Shared Ground Rule
rules.body: The window, status bar, navigation bar, action bar, browser toolbar and page all paint `ground`, so the app reads as one surface. app.css and colors.xml carry the same value for the same name in each scheme; a token added on one side takes the other side's value.

rules.name: The Four Sizes Rule
rules.body: Every piece of text sits on one of four sizes 1.2 apart: 12.5, 15, 18 and 21.6px, the same values in sp natively. A fifth size is a bug.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Address Rule
rules.body: Monospace sets addresses and hashes only, never labels, counts or headings; numbers in the sans use tabular figures instead.

rules.name: The 48 Floor Rule
rules.body: Every touch target is at least 48px (48dp). When the visual is smaller, the hit area grows and the shape does not: a 40px chip's input reaches 4px above and below it, and 48px icon buttons sit 12px into the margin so their glyphs align with the text edge.

rules.name: The Flat Night Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and separated by tone and 1px hairlines. The focus ring is the only coloured shadow, status dots carry no halos, and the glow belongs to the icon art alone.

rules.name: The Pill Carries State Rule
rules.body: Fully rounded shapes are kept for things that show or set state: chips, the trust strip, route badges and the address pill. Actions are 14px rounded rectangles and surfaces 16px; a pill-shaped button breaks the language.

rules.name: The In-Place Rule
rules.body: Results replace each other where they stand: rows already showing stay still, only new rows fade in (from 0.4 opacity, 4px lower, over 220ms), there is no spinner, and skeleton rows appear only when the index takes more than 150ms.

dos: Do keep a network's hue to its 8px dot, its route badge (the hue at 14% behind 12.5px/600 hue text) and the browser's kind label.
Do show selection with the one accent treatment on every network: accent at 13% over surface, a border of accent 45% into line, ink text and a 16px accent check.
Do make every touch target at least 48px (48dp); when the visual is smaller, as with the 40px chips, extend the hit area instead of the shape.
Do paint the window, system bars, action bar, browser toolbar and page with the same `ground`, and give a new colour the same value in app.css and colors.xml for each scheme.
Do set addresses in mono at 12.5px on one ellipsised line, with onion hosts shortened to both ends, and set counts, timings and dates in tabular figures.
Do divide list items with 1px `line` hairlines and let tone (ground, surface, surface-2) carry depth.
Do draw icons on a 24-unit grid with a 1.75 stroke, round caps and joins and no fill, stepping the stroke up only below 20px.
Do keep motion short and decelerating (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), 160 to 240ms), update results in place, and turn all motion off under reduced motion.
Do use the accent vector rings for the brand mark on the light ground and the glowing raster on the dark ground.
donts: Don't fill a chip, tint a row, or colour a button or border with a network hue.
Don't add coloured glow shadows or halos to UI elements or status dots; the 4px focus ring is the only coloured shadow, and the glow belongs to the icon art.
Don't put results or Explore sites in cards.
Don't add a text size off the four-step ramp, or a web font: the page's content policy loads nothing from outside its own origin.
Don't use mono for anything but addresses and hashes.
Don't use the `glow` token as a fill; it marks focus, the caret and progress only.
Don't show a spinner while searching.
Don't give the action bar or browser toolbar a colour band or elevation of its own.
